Walter Hagen. The Haig. An American professional golfer who won 11 major championships and became the first true professional superstar of golf. His charismatic personality, business acumen, and competitive dominance in the 1920s established the template for the modern professional golfer.

He won 11 major championships: 2 US Opens in 1914 and 1919, 5 PGA Championships from 1921 to 1927, and 4 Open Championships in 1922, 1924, 1928, and 1929. Dominating the 1920s, he won at least one major championship every year from 1921 to 1927—an extraordinary streak of dominance. Hagen was the first golfer to openly play as a professional without apology, elevating the status of professional golf and breaking down the amateur-only establishment. He was known for his flamboyant lifestyle, showmanship, and ability to perform under pressure—qualities that made him a celebrity. He won 45 professional tournaments, establishing himself as a prolific winner across multiple decades.

Hagen pioneered the concept of the golf celebrity through endorsements, exhibitions, and world tours, establishing the business model for professional golfers. He reached the finals of the PGA Championship 5 consecutive times from 1923 to 1927, demonstrating sustained excellence. He succeeded where many athletes fail: maintaining relevance and affection across changing eras, from the 1920s through the 21st century.
